# Provide upgrades more frequently (AH-0MVCFB00Y004AQ2Z)

## Problem statement

When the player's hold fills and they are offered a choice of power-ups and
weapons, items the player already owns (i.e. level-up offers) currently appear
only **10% more often** (1.1× weight) than unowned items. That bias is too weak:
players report/builds feel like they are constantly chasing new items instead of
steadily upgrading the build they already have. Owned items should appear
**25% more often** than unowned ones.

## Users

- **Player (progression):** "As a player, when the hold-full choice opens I want
  upgrades for items I already own to appear noticeably more often, so my build
  keeps improving rather than forcing me to collect new items."
- **Designer / balance owner:** "As a designer I want owned upgrades to be 25%
  more likely to appear so progression feels steady and an existing build is
  rewarded."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — 25% weighting.** Owned level-up offers (`weapon-level` and
  `power-up-level`) receive a **1.25×** weight multiplier during candidate
  selection; unowned (base-pool) items retain 1.0×. Interpreted as the natural
  extension of the existing convention: "10% more likely" = 1.1×, therefore
  "25% more likely" = 1.25× (multiplicative, not +25 percentage points).
- **AC2 — Single source of truth.** The new value is the named constant
  `OWNED_UPGRADE_BONUS_WEIGHT` in `src/powerups/choice.ts` — no magic numbers,
  and no copy of the weighting anywhere else.
- **AC3 — Gym↔game parity.** Behaviour is identical in `PlayScene` and every
  gym that opens the hold-full choice (they share `src/powerups/choice.ts` and
  `MineralChoiceScene`); the repo-wide duplicate-body/parity guards still pass.
- **AC4 — Testing/validation.** Tests updated so the full suite is green:
  (a) the constant asserts 1.25; (b) unit tests assert owned candidates weigh
  1.25× and unowned 1.0×; (c) the deterministic weighted-draw test and the
  10,000-trial distribution test are recalibrated to the 1.25 / 2.25 weighted
  probability (tolerance band ±3% retained); (d) the docs-guard test
  (`src/choiceWeightingDocs.test.ts`) reflects 1.25× / 25%.
- **AC5 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
  change: code comments in `src/powerups/choice.ts`, `README.md` (§
  `src/powerups/choice.ts` description), and `docs/Game Design Document.md`
  (§4.5 hold-full choice and the architecture diagram line recording 1.1×),
  plus `docs/BALANCING.md` if it mentions the owned-upgrade weights.
- **AC6 — Full suite.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
  (CI/CD pipeline tests are out of scope.)

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md):** the shared behaviour lives once in
  `src/powerups/choice.ts` and is consumed by the game and every gym — this
  change only edits that shared module and its docs/tests.
- **Backward compatible:** no breaking changes to the `ChoiceStrategy`
  interface or `ChoiceOption` shape; only the selection probabilities shift.
- **Run-scoped:** no persistence or leaderboard impact.
- **Wording transparency:** player-facing copy should continue to describe the
  items, not the odds — the 25% bias is a selection-policy detail, not UI copy.

## Existing state

`OWNED_UPGRADE_BONUS_WEIGHT = 1.1` in `src/powerups/choice.ts` (added by
AH-0MUY47W62005FF74, shipped in v0.1.11). The weighted selection lives in
`drawWeightedWithoutReplacement` inside `createRandomChoiceStrategy`; owned
`weapon-level`/`power-up-level` offers get the 1.1× weight while unowned base
entries get 1.0×. Docs guard `src/choiceWeightingDocs.test.ts` pins 1.1× /
"10% more likely" in `README.md` and the GDD — any value change requires those
documents to move in lockstep or the guard fails.

## Desired change

- Change `OWNED_UPGRADE_BONUS_WEIGHT` from `1.1` to `1.25` in
  `src/powerups/choice.ts`, updating the doc comments ("10%" → "25%").
- Recalibrate unit tests (`src/powerups/__tests__/choice.test.ts`):
  constant assertion, weight assertions, the deterministic draw expectation
  (with total weight 2.25, r=0.48 → threshold 1.08 still crosses the 1.0
  unowned weight and lands on the owned level-up — verify the comment and
  thresholds hold), and the 10,000-trial ±3% distribution test against the
  theoretical 1.25 / 2.25 probability (still well within ±3%).
- Update the docs guard (`src/choiceWeightingDocs.test.ts`) and the documents
  it asserts: `README.md` and `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§4.5 + diagram
  row) from 1.1×/10% to 1.25×/25%.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — `OWNED_UPGRADE_BONUS_WEIGHT` 1.1 → 1.25 and doc comments.
- `src/powerups/__tests__/choice.test.ts` — constant assertion, weight assertions, deterministic-draw test, 10,000-trial distribution test.
- `src/choiceWeightingDocs.test.ts` — docs guard pinned to the old 1.1×/10% values.
- `README.md` — § `src/powerups/choice.ts` description ("1.1×" / "10% more often").
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.5 hold-full choice and architecture-diagram row ("1.1×" / "10% more likely").

## Related work

- **AH-0MUY47W62005FF74 (completed)** — Add 10% weighting to owned upgrades in
  hold-full choice. Direct antecedent: introduced `OWNED_UPGRADE_BONUS_WEIGHT`
  and the "X% more likely = (1 + X/100)×" convention; this item retunes the same
  knob from 10% to 25%.
- **AH-0MUVRACE9001WVT2 (completed)** — Level-up offers duplicate weapon; the
  de-duplication in `buildChoiceCandidates` this weighting operates on.
- **AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR (completed)** — Show upgrade change summary and New
  badge in the hold-full choice list (display metadata; unaffected).
- **AH-0MV8QT7CB0060A7A (open)** — Extend the headless arena to simulate the
  full shipped campaign (find-related match); the retuned weighting is one of
  the tunables the headless arena would eventually cover.
- **AH-0MV55OC080068H03 (completed)** — Full-suite verification: typecheck,
  tests and build; this item reruns the full suite to confirm green.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** "25% more likely" is a 1.25× **multiplicative** weight,
  consistent with the documented 1.1× interpretation of "10% more likely"
  (AH-0MUY47W62005FF74). If an additive interpretation (+25pp) were intended,
  the weight would instead be 1.667× — flagged for producer confirmation, but
  the multiplicative reading is the established convention.
- **Statistical tolerance (low):** the 10,000-trial ±3% test remains valid for
  1.25/2.25 (≈55.6% expected probability).
- **Docs-guard coupling (low):** forgetting to update README/GDD fails
  `src/choiceWeightingDocs.test.ts` — mechanically caught, not a silent risk.
- **Scope creep (low):** this item is a single-constant retune plus its
  docs/tests. Steering by player-input weighting (e.g. "favour the item the
  player picked least") is out of scope; record as a follow-up item if wanted.
- **Assumption:** "Hull full plugins" in the seed description is a
  transcription of "hold-full power-ups"; weapons items = owned weapon drops.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interview questions were required: the seed description, the direct 10%
precedent (AH-0MUY47W62005FF74) and repo search fully determined the scope
(change `OWNED_UPGRADE_BONUS_WEIGHT` 1.1 → 1.25 and keep docs/tests in
lockstep). The one interpretive decision (multiplicative 1.25× vs additive) is
recorded above as an assumption following the established convention.

# 10-wave campaign data foundation

Extend the campaign data so every level has exactly 10 waves with wave 10 marked as the mini-boss wave, keeping the fixed/dynamic authoring mix (epic AH-0MVCC8XSS007P01Z).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` has exactly 10 rows per level 1–10 (100 waves).
2. Targets are non-decreasing across the 100 rows; wave 10 of each level carries a mini-boss marker/`generation` mode consumable by the WaveManager.
3. `Formations.ts` `LEVELS`/`sequencedLevels.ts` expose 10 waves per level with the 10th as the mini-boss wave; existing fixed/dynamic showcase waves are preserved.
4. `defaultDifficultyCurves()` in `src/core/configStore.ts` records the 10-wave curves; the F1 harness goes green for this feature's scope.
5. Wave-10 target difficulty sits above each level's regular waves but below the following level's opening.

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` (+ `defaultDifficultyCurves()`).
- Add wave-10 mini-boss entries to `LEVELS` in `src/waves/Formations.ts`.
- Update any level-count/`HARVESTER_*` ranges as needed.
- Deliverable: data-driven 10-wave campaign.

**Key Files:** `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv`, `src/waves/Formations.ts`, `src/core/configStore.ts`, `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts`
**Dependencies:** Verification harness (AH-0MVCRAHWO0007US2). **Deliverables:** 100-wave data; falling into F1.

# Guard test: audio balance invariants (AC5)

**Parent:** Balance the levels of all enemy sounds (AH-0MVAUU594007S92Q)

Create a guard test that asserts the two key amplitude/scale invariants over every enemy cue in the ToneForge manifest, preventing silent regression of the balance work.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] ] **AC5 — Validation, docs, full suite:** a guard test asserts AC2 + AC3 over every enemy entry in `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` (via the audio build/verify path, e.g. extended `build-audio` verification) and passes with the new assets (`npm run build-audio:verify`); all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes (recipe amplitude tiers + scale table in `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`, README/guide references, code comments); the full project test suite and `npm run build` (including the audio render + checksum update) pass.

- Guard test reads `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` and identifies every enemy cue
- Guard test asserts AC2 amplitude targets: each rendered WAV amplitude (RMS or peak) sits within the documented category tier (±1.5 dB; peak ≤ 0.50), no clipping
- Guard test asserts AC3 scale conformance: every pitched oscillator automation point (start/end/waypoint frequency) in enemy recipes is an A natural minor note (scale-degree variants allowed), noise-only cues exempt as documented
- Guard test runs as part of `npm run build-audio:verify` (extend `scripts/build-audio.test.ts` or a new guard module)
- Guard test is deterministic and reasonably fast
- Test passes with the rebalanced assets; it is expected to fail before recipes are rebalanced

**Deliverables:**

- New or extended test file for audio balance invariants
- Integrated into build-audio:verify pipeline

**Dependencies:** None (created test-first; will fail until recipes are balanced and re-rendered)

data.comment: Plan auto-complete: sufficiently sized/defined for direct implementation. Effort Extra Small / Risk Medium flagged the item for planning, but Process Step 1 applies — this is a single atomic retune (constant 1.1 → 1.25 in src/powerups/choice.ts) where the constant, unit tests, docs guard and docs must move in lockstep (no green intermediate state), so child decomposition would create non-viable slices. Six automated review stages completed: (1) AC alignment — AC1-AC6 all trace to the problem statement; (2) completeness — description has goal, ACs, Key Files (validated syntactically, all accurate); (3) sequencing — atomic change, tests embedded in AC4/A C5; (4) scope sizing — Extra Small single increment; (5) testability — all ACs measurable (1.25× weight, deterministic draw r=0.48→1.08, 1.25/2.25 distribution); (6) polish — actionable. Coverage review: 100% AC coverage, no gaps, no children needed (recommendation: proceed).
